title: `AnimationTree` breaks animations under specific circumstances
body:
### Tested versions

I tested it in:
- v4.6.1.stable.mono.official [14d19694e]
- v4.5.stable.mono.official [876b29033]

Happens in both.

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 680M (radeonsi, rembrandt, LLVM 21.1.8, DRM 3.64, 6.18.9-200.fc43.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen 7 6800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 14.85 GiB memory

### Issue description

Under some specific circumstances, `AnimationTree` will mess up my animations and the only way I have found so far to solve it is to assing its `AnimationPlayer`'s `current_animation` property to `"RESET"` on ready.

> By "mess up" I mean mainly skipping some animated properties, although I've also found it behabing in unexpected ways depending on its internal structure. But skipping animated properties is the recurring issue.

I did some testing trying to find out what these circumstances were, but got inconsistent results. Therefore, even though I have some clues, I will not claim to have a triggering cause for this bug, as that would probably be nothing but misleading.

Observe the difference in the animations of my character before and after not setting the `AnimationPlayer`property on ready:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d6dcef7-402f-4196-8f04-039504c45fe2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Download and import my MRP below to Godot.
2. Play `scene.tscn` and observe how the bird's animations play correctly. Play each different animation using 1–4 keys.
3. Open `controller.gd` and comment `_ready` function and its content.
4. Play the scene again, navigate the birds animations and observe how they aren't played correctly anymore.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The MRP shown in the previows video: [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25502852/MessedAnimationTree.zip)
